subject: language
intro: I'm Ms. Alvarez. Let's plan a 6th grade lesson on determining the central idea of an informational text.

beats.narration: Students know the phrase "big idea," so I use it before introducing "central idea."
This standard asks students to determine a central idea and how it is conveyed through details.
Central idea and supporting details are always taught together.
beats.text: Students will be able to determine the central idea of an informational article and identify three supporting details.

beats.narration: The table metaphor is simple and sticks.
beats.text: Show a table (the central idea) with legs (details). "What happens if you remove a leg?"

beats.narration: The "not stated directly" point prevents students from just copying the first sentence.
beats.text: Model with a short article: read, annotate key details, and look for what they all have in common. Show how the central idea is often not stated directly.

beats.narration: Comparing with another pair shows there's more than one good way to phrase it.
beats.text: Partners read a new article, annotate details, and write a central idea statement. Then they compare with another pair and revise.
What is the central idea of today's article? List two details that support it.

outro: Metaphor, model, practice, compare. Your turn.
